title: Fix interval merging boundary bug
prompt: You are working in the current directory. There is a file `intervals.py` containing a function `merge_intervals(intervals)` that is supposed to merge a list of `(start, end)` integer intervals (inclusive bounds, start <= end) into the smallest possible sorted list of non-overlapping, non-touching intervals. Two intervals are considered mergeable if they overlap OR merely touch (e.g. (1, 3) and (3, 5) must merge into (1, 5), since 3 is shared). The current implementation has a bug that causes some intervals which should be merged to be left separate. Find and fix the bug in `intervals.py` so that `merge_intervals` always returns a correctly merged, sorted list for any valid input (including unsorted input, a single interval, an empty list, and intervals fully contained within another interval). Do not change the function's name or signature. Run `python -m pytest tests_visible -q` to check your work; note that the visible tests only cover a subset of behavior, so make sure your fix matches the full description above, not just the visible tests.
